s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent skin fragility with seasonal variation and superficial erosions
salient_findings: Superficial skin erosions with linear geographic contour
Lesions predominantly located at areas of friction
key_facts: Symptoms improved in winter and worsened in summer
Physical and mental developments were normal
Mild xerosis with superficial skin erosions
Erythematous residual macules from previous erosions
Hair, nails, and mucous membranes were normal
No history of blistering
Serological markers for celiac disease were negative
Hematoxylin-eosin staining showed complete separation of the stratum corneum
Genetic study revealed 2 heterozygous mutations in exon 2 of the CDSN gene

differentials: Focal palmoplantar keratoderma with oral mucosal hyperpigmentation
Corneal dystrophy and perceptive deafness syndrome

Congenital hemidysplasia with ichthyosiform erythroderma and limb defects

shortlist.label: Peeling skin syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of skin fragility, superficial erosions, and seasonal variation matches this condition

shortlist.label: Acral peeling skin syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical features and genetic mutations in the CDSN gene support this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Samira type peeling skin syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Shared characteristics of peeling skin and superficial erosions, although less common, make it a plausible consideration

shortlist.label: Keratolysis exfoliativa
shortlist.why_kept: Seasonal variation and superficial skin erosions are consistent with this condition, but genetic findings and other clinical features are less typical

shortlist.label: Generalized peeling skin syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: While the clinical presentation overlaps, the lack of specific genetic mutations and less distinctive features make it a less likely but still possible diagnosis

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of skin fragility, superficial skin erosions, and improvement in winter and worsening in summer, along with the genetic study revealing 2 heterozygous mutations in exon 2 of the CDSN gene, are consistent with peeling skin syndrome.

rejected.label: Acral peeling skin syndrome
rejected.why: The lesions are not limited to acral areas, but are predominantly located at areas of friction

rejected.label: Samira type peeling skin syndrome
rejected.why: There is no specific information provided that matches the characteristics of Samira type peeling skin syndrome

rejected.label: Keratolysis exfoliativa
rejected.why: The condition is not limited to the palms and soles, and the histopathological findings do not match keratolysis exfoliativa

rejected.label: Generalized peeling skin syndrome
rejected.why: While the patient has widespread skin involvement, the specific genetic mutations and histopathological findings are more consistent with peeling skin syndrome
